head: 867092c5b379a696e5ea7a5d6164aef9d5000a80
summary: Both readers in eng/rules-parity.ps1 are now closed grammars that classify every line, instead of lists of refused shapes. Yaml (O-023): before `rules:` only comments and blank lines are allowed. After it, indentation must be ASCII spaces, so U+00A0, U+3000 and tab are refused, and only comments and `  - name: ` entry starts may sit at indent 0-3. A twinned entry is a single-quoted name, then bare identifier keys at indent 4 from a fixed set, each at most once. The list keys take single-quoted items at one indent; the other keys take one single-quoted scalar, or true or false. The settled marker must stand between entries. C# (O-024): a lexer refuses block comments, preprocessor directives, raw strings, strings that run onto the next line, and literals inside interpolation holes. The file may hold only its two prologue lines and one type, and every attribute must be `[Fact]` or `[Theory]` alone on its line. A Fact's body is `{`, one AssertNoMatch( call and `}`. The files argument may use only a fixed word list. AssertNoMatch is named once per Fact and declared once, and the declared body is pinned. C-005 gained 18 rows under both shells (262 checks in all, 0 failed). On the reviewer's seven M4/M5 shapes the committed reader gave AGREE, exit 0; the new one refuses each with exit 2. The real tree still AGREEs, Core.Tests passes 120/120, and harness cases C-007 and C-008 pass.

files.why: O-023: Read-Entries rewritten as a closed grammar over the whole yaml file (prologue, ASCII-space indentation, indent 0-3 shapes, marker between entries, per-entry key grammar with no duplicate keys and a fixed key set, one-line single-quoted scalars). O-024: new Get-CsCode lexer, type and prologue check, attribute-line check, closed Fact-body grammar ({, one call, }), files-argument word list, and the AssertNoMatch declaration count and body pin. The header describes both grammars.

O-023/O-024: 18 C-005 rows, each requiring CANNOT-READ at its line under powershell.exe and pwsh. Yaml: 5 duplicate must_not_match spellings (bare, single-quoted, double-quoted, tagged, ? explicit), must_not_import, a deeper line after a scalar key, a plain value, a marker inside a list, a key before rules:, and U+00A0/U+3000/tab-led keys. C#: a second qualified call, a call behind if (true), return before the call, a statement after it, a files argument that reads files, an interpolated files argument, a Fact in a block comment, #if, a one-line Fact, a nested class, a second AssertNoMatch declaration, a changed AssertNoMatch body, and an extra using.

obligations.how: Built the closed grammar the fix specified: (1) a non-space leading whitespace char is refused (`^ *[^\S ]`), and nothing but comments and entry starts sits at indent 0-3; (2) twinned lines at indent 4 must be bare identifier keys `^    [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*:`, each at most once, from name/files/except_files/must_not_match/including_comments/because; (3) the marker counts only if the lines after it up to the next entry start are blank or comments, else 'the settled marker sits inside an entry'. Settled entries are only counted, as the decision required. C-005 rows cover (a) the bare, single-quoted, double-quoted, tagged and `?` duplicate keys, (b) the marker inside the list, and (c) U+00A0, U+3000 and tab. Each gives CANNOT-READ at its line under both shells. The committed reader gave AGREE, exit 0, on the quoted, `?`, marker and U+00A0 shapes.

Read-Facts now requires `{` alone on a line after the signature, allows only blank and // lines before the AssertNoMatch( call and between the call's `);` and the `}` at the `{`'s indent, and refuses a second AssertNoMatch anywhere in the body. The body ends at its own `}`, so the helper's declaration is not inside the last Fact. C-005 rows for (a) the qualified second call, (b) the call behind `if (true)` and (c) `return;` before the call give CANNOT-READ at :72, :72 and :70 under both shells; the committed reader gave AGREE, exit 0, on all three. I also closed the rest of the Fact grammar: a lexer, one type, whole-line attributes, a files-argument word list, and the AssertNoMatch declaration count and body pin. Each has a C-005 row (see deviations).

Owed to validate-slice, and not changed this attempt. Attempt 1 ran the full harness three times with the same verdict for every row. This attempt touches only the parity readers; C-007 (clean scenario, parity first) and C-008 (16 plants plus both scope bites) still pass.

deviations: The C# closure goes beyond the three shapes O-024 named. The design took it as given that AssertNoMatch applies RegexOptions.Multiline to each pattern as passed, and that the reflected Fact count is enough to keep the reader's Facts and xUnit's Facts the same. Neither held against a closed reading. A Fact in a block comment, or behind #if, plus a one-line or nested-class Fact, keeps the counts equal while xUnit runs a pattern parity never reads. A second AssertNoMatch overload, or an edit to its body, changes what every pattern means to xUnit. So the reader now also refuses block comments, preprocessor directives, raw and multi-line strings, any type other than the test class, any attribute not alone on its line, and a files argument using words outside a fixed list. It pins AssertNoMatch's declaration and body. Each has a C-005 row. The pin means a deliberate change to AssertNoMatch must update the copy in eng/rules-parity.ps1 in the same change.

The zero-Facts check moved into Read-Facts, before the new attribute-line rule, so the existing '[Fect]' row still reads 'zero [Fact]s found'. The bare-dash and column-0 messages from O-020/O-021 are kept word for word.
follow_ups: What parity still cannot see: the closed grammar covers the text of the two files, not what their names resolve to. A type named Regex added to namespace FsAnalyser.Core.Tests in another file, or a global using alias, changes what the pinned AssertNoMatch does without either file changing. The Files helper, which only chooses files, is deliberately not pinned. Only the behavioural harness sees these.

The files-argument word list (Files, Except, Concat, Where, StartsWith, f, StringComparison, OrdinalIgnoreCase) is the current file's vocabulary. A Fact rescoped with, say, EndsWith gets CANNOT-READ until the list in eng/rules-parity.ps1 is extended. That is intended, but the person editing a rule will meet it.

Loop observation: build-slice attempts 1-4 were each taken back as WRONG by code review for the same defect class, a spelling the line reader neither read nor refused (M1-M5, m1). Each changed only eng/rules-parity.ps1 and the case runner. This attempt replaces the patching with closed grammars on both readers. If the next review still finds a shape, the design-level alternative is worth weighing: have the harness (which has the engine) compare Fitness's parsed rules with parity's reading, where the engine is available.
